summary: Insurance Product Information Document (IPID) for easyPROTECT-Auto, a Luxembourg motor vehicle insurance for cars and camping vans distributed under the LALUX Assurances brand. It covers motor third party liability and damage caused to the insured vehicle, and is sold as four cumulative tiers: BASISC RATE (as printed), SECURITY = Basic rate plus fire, theft, glass breakage, collision with a stray animal, forces of nature and an optional total loss guarantee; COMFORT = SECURITY plus damage to the vehicle and a replacement vehicle; PERFORMANCE = COMFORT plus personalisation of the premium and Repairs plus. Optional accessory guarantees (replacement value for three years, purchase value of used vehicle) apply to SECURITY (excl. total loss), COMFORT and PERFORMANCE, and luggage, accident coverage and the driver guarantee are listed for all packages.

gaps: Risk carrier undeterminable from this document. The header band prints only the brand "LALUX Assurances - Product : easyPROTECT-Auto" (verified on a 4x render of the page-1 band) and the body refers to the risk carrier only as "the company" / "the insurance company". No legal form, no R.C.S. number, no registered address and no supervisor appear on either page. lalux distributes under two separately authorised entities, and this document does not allow a choice between them, so no carrier entity has been recorded. `insurer_name` records the printed brand "LALUX Assurances" rather than the task-metadata value "lalux"; `insurer_slug` is copied through from the task metadata unchanged.

`edition_date` is null: no edition date, version code, year or printed footer appears on either page. Verified on renders; the lower margins carry only the "Non-exhaustive list" mentions and the disclaimer. Nothing was promoted from the file name or from PDF file metadata. `reference` is null for the same reason.

`target_audience` is null and `target_audience_note` is null: the document nowhere states a market segment. It describes the risk ("Motor vehicle insurance – cars and camping vans") and mentions a "young driver" and "members of the policyholder's family", but never says whether it is sold to particuliers, independants or entreprises. The audience was deliberately not deduced from the product type.

File-name divergence, recorded not resolved. The source file name contains "vehicules-type-1" (vehicle type 1). No vehicle-type category, class or numbering appears anywhere in the printed document, which describes itself only as "Motor vehicle insurance – cars and camping vans". Nothing has been promoted from the file name into any field. Sibling language versions of the same file name were not consulted.

Bullet marks are bitmap images, not text and not vector drawings. `page.get_text("text")` returns a bare tab plus space where each bullet sits, and `page.get_drawings()` carries no marks. Membership was recovered from the image blocks of `get_text("dict")` and placed by coordinate, then settled on a 3x-4x render. Counts close exactly on page 1: 31 image blocks = 20 green ticks in "What is insured  ?" (15 at x0 29.8 in the left column, 5 at x0 307.6 at the top of the right column) + 5 red crosses at x0 307.6 (y 426-556) in "What is not insured ?" + 6 orange exclamation marks at x0 309.5 (y 645-769) in "Are there any restrictions on cover ?". Page 2 carries 2 further green ticks in "Where am I covered ?". The 20 ticks map onto 18 named guarantees because "Theft and attempted theft" and "Glass breakage*" each carry two bullets. These counts are stated here and not in `key_quotes`, because image marks are not text and cannot be grounded.

Two-column reversal check run and NEGATIVE. Page 1 is a two-column layout (left column x0 29.8, right column x0 307.6). The flat text emits the left column in full before the right column, and within the right column top-to-bottom, so covered items, exclusions and restrictions all attach to the correct box; nothing is crossed. Confirmed on a render: green ticks mark the insured box, red crosses the not-insured box, orange exclamation marks the restrictions box, so polarity is carried by three visually distinct marks and not by proximity alone. One flow-order artifact exists and is harmless: the full-width "Disclaimer" band (y 130.7-169.1) and the "What type of insurance is it ?" band (y 180.6-224.8) are printed at the TOP of page 1, above the two columns, but are emitted LAST in the flat text. They carry no coverage or exclusion, so no value is mis-attached; their `page` is still 1.

Internal tension between two boxes, recorded rather than resolved. "Driver guarantee" is listed under "For all packages:" in the "What is insured  ?" box, while the "Are there any restrictions on cover ?" box states for civil liability "Damage to the driver: only optional". The document does not reconcile the two. Both readings are recorded verbatim - the guarantee is kept in `coverages` with `is_optional: null`, and the restriction is kept as an exclusion - and neither has been silently preferred.

Printed typography preserved verbatim, not corrected. The first package heading prints "BASISC RATE" (verified on a 4x render of the page-1 band - the page really does print BASISC, not BASIC); "COMFORT =SECURITY + the following items :" is printed without a space after the equals sign; "Lightning strike, burns, short circuit, etc.." ends with two full stops; and "Costs and fees, up to EUR 10,000, of any proceedings or proceedings following a traffic accident" repeats the word "proceedings". None of these has been repaired, so the quotes remain exact spans of the text layer.

The document uses thin spaces (U+2009) inside "Product : easyPROTECT-Auto", "What is insured  ?", "What is not insured ?", "Are there any restrictions on cover ?" and "SECURITY = Basic rate + the following items :", and a curly apostrophe (U+2019) in "policyholder's family" and "the company's consent". Every `key_quotes` entry was sliced programmatically out of the PyMuPDF text layer rather than retyped, so those characters are preserved exactly.

Amounts are printed with the ISO code and a comma thousands separator ("EUR 10,000", "EUR 2,500", "EUR 500") and are kept verbatim in that form. No euro sign appears anywhere in the document, so there is no missing-glyph problem here; the unit is spelled as "EUR" on the page.

`is_optional` is only set where the document itself says so: true for "Legal protection (for an additional premium)", "Optional guarantee – Total loss" and the two "Optional accessory guarantee" items, false for "Civil liability" which sits in the BASISC RATE tier. It is left null for every guarantee whose availability depends only on which cumulative package is bought (SECURITY / COMFORT / PERFORMANCE), because the document states tier membership, not optionality, for those. The governing tier heading is recorded verbatim in each coverage's `conditions`.

`definitions` is empty: the document contains no glossary or defined terms. `waiting_periods` is empty and `prescription_period` is null: neither is mentioned. `deductibles.standard` and `deductibles.variable` are null - the only franchise wording in the document is "Recent licence deductible; not deductible if the contract is in the name of a young driver", which states no amount.

The "Are there any restrictions on cover ?" box has been recorded in `exclusions` (6 items) alongside the 5 items of the "What is not insured ?" box, because the schema has no separate restrictions array. Each description names the box it came from, so the two can be told apart downstream; the box headings and the per-guarantee sub-headings are reproduced verbatim.

The text layer of the page-1 header band is set in white (colour 16777215); it is printed on a solid blue banner and is fully legible on a render, so this is normal reversed-out type and not hidden text.

Both `coverages` and `exclusions` are exhaustive for this document: every bullet printed in the three boxes is recorded, and the tick/cross/exclamation counts above confirm none was dropped. The document itself declares all three lists "Non-exhaustive list", i.e. the underlying policy has more than the IPID prints; that statement is recorded in `special_conditions` and nothing has been added from outside the document.
